$comment: Spec State Object — the single shared memory across all agents in the UX Spec Generation System. Initialize a copy of this template for each new feature spec.

$conventions.$comment: Authoring rules that MUST be honored when any agent or command writes to this object. These are contract, not decoration.

timestamps.rule: Every `created_at`, `last_updated`, audit-event `timestamp`, `resolved_at`, `chosen_at`, gate `approved_at`, and `*_at` field MUST be a REAL wall-clock ISO-8601 timestamp captured at the moment the action occurred (e.g., 2026-07-01T15:42:09Z).
forbidden: Synthetic placeholders like 'T00:00:01', 'T00:00:0N', or monotonic fake sequences — these make iteration duration unmeasurable and are a protocol violation.

Using `last_updated` (or any timestamp field) to carry a STATUS STRING (e.g. last_updated: 'in review'). Status lives in `phase.status` / `gates.*.status` / `run_status`; timestamps carry only ISO datetimes.

audit_event_vocabulary.$comment: CLOSED set. `audit_log[]` entries MUST use exactly one of these `event` values. Do not invent new event strings; if no value fits, the action probably should not be logged or the vocabulary needs a deliberate revision.

entry_shape.event: one of the closed vocabulary above
entry_shape.phase: integer 0–7 or null when not phase-scoped
entry_shape.details: object — event-specific payload (e.g., {from, to} for scope_change; {clarification_id, chosen, chosen_via, user_message_ref} for clarification_resolved; {justification} for gate_bypassed)

scope_lock.$comment: Locked at Phase 1 intake (event: scope_locked) and RE-CONFIRMED before Phase 3. Any later change to a locked field is a deliberate `scope_change` audit event with rationale — never a silent rerun. Read by the orchestrator at Phase 1 close and at Phase 3 open.

phase.$run_status_comment: active | paused | abandoned | complete. Set `abandoned` (with a run_abandoned audit event) when a run is left incomplete rather than leaving a silent gap. Set `complete` after Phase 7 gate approval.

phase_1.name: Problem Statement Approval
artifact_checklist: Intake clarifications recorded (or bulk-accepted)
BLUF problem statement (≤ 3 sentences)
Affected user roles identified
Current workaround and failure mode documented
Compliance risk if unaddressed
Out-of-scope adjacent problems listed
Clarifying questions answered by PM/stakeholders
Assumptions validated or flagged for research

phase_2.name: Research Brief Approval
artifact_checklist: Relevant NIST/DoD control IDs identified with [SOURCE] citations
UX implication documented per control
Competitive landscape analyzed (minimum 3 platforms)
Patterns to leverage identified
Patterns to avoid/adapt for classified environments identified
Differentiation opportunities documented
Research gaps flagged

phase_3.name: PRD Approval
artifact_checklist: Executive Summary in BLUF format
User stories by role with acceptance criteria
Functional requirements numbered and testable
Non-functional requirements with specific control citations
Success metrics quantified
Out of scope with reasoning
Dependencies listed with blockers flagged
All [VERIFY WITH PM] items resolved
Threat model reviewed — no unmitigated P1 risks
Pre-flight review passed — no vague/unmeasurable requirements

phase_4.name: Solution Direction Approval
artifact_checklist: Minimum 3 distinct solution approaches documented
Evaluation matrix completed (7 criteria scored)
BLUF recommendation with justification
Top 3 risks of recommended approach with mitigations
Trade-offs explicitly stated
Approach aligns with compliance constraints from Phase 2

phase_5.name: Flow Approval
artifact_checklist: All PRD user stories have corresponding flows
Error paths documented for all flows
Security audit passed — no bypass vectors
Navigation patterns consistent with existing Mattermost UX
Mobile flows documented or explicitly marked desktop-only
Feedback disposition recorded ((a) real w/ sources / (b) labeled synthetic / (c) none w/ reason)

phase_7.name: UX Spec Approval
artifact_checklist: All REQUIRED template sections populated; INCLUDE-WHEN-NEEDED sections only when they add value (menu model)
Edge case review completed — all P1 findings resolved (internal validation, not a separate appendix)
Internal traceability check passed — PRD requirements covered; gaps justified
No unresolved [TBD] items remain
All open questions have owners and target dates
Roles & Permissions documented when the permission model is non-trivial
Accessibility documented for non-standard interactions
Analytics events defined when PM requests tracking
Compliance appendix attached for Tier 1 / access-control features
Mobile behavior explicitly documented (parity or differences)

artifacts.$wireframe_review_comment: holds per-direction flow audit output (key name retained for compatibility)

$open_questions_item_schema.$comment: Each entry in `open_questions[]` is a TYPED object of this shape — not a bare string. `[VERIFY WITH PM]` blockers live here. The decide-or-fork checkpoint (before Phase 5/6) reads `status`; any item still `open` with a load-bearing blocker must be decided or explicitly branched before the checkpoint passes.
$open_questions_item_schema.owner: pm | eng | design | security | <name> — who must resolve it
$open_questions_item_schema.blocker: true when this is a load-bearing [VERIFY WITH PM] that gates Phase 5/6; false for non-blocking tracking
$open_questions_item_schema.phase_ref: P<N> — the phase that raised it
$open_questions_item_schema.resolution: the decision text, or the branch rationale when status=branched, or the defer rationale when status=deferred
$open_questions_item_schema.branch_spec_ref: when status=branched: the sibling spec slug the alternative was forked into (never a silent same-day fork)

context.$verify_decision_checkpoints_comment: Records each pre-Phase-5 / pre-Phase-6 decide-or-fork checkpoint: {at_phase, timestamp, blockers_reviewed:[V-ids], outcome: 'all_decided' | 'branched', notes}. The orchestrator appends one here (and a verify_decision_checkpoint audit event) every time the checkpoint runs.
